newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS BEAT DEVILS FOR FIRST WIN OF SEASON AT HOME.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS BEAT DEVILS FOR FIRST WIN OF SEASON AT HOME.

text.p: Adam Oates had a goal and two assists and the Boston Bruins scored three times in a 2:07 span in the first period for their first home win, 5-2 over the New Jersey Devils Tuesday.
Boston cruised to the win despite being outshot 48-33, including 23-8 in the third period.
Todd Elik's second goal opened the scoring 5:44 into the game. Steve Heinze's sixth goal gave Boston a 2-0 lead just 71 seconds later, and Oates scored to make it 3-0.

Reese allowed four goals on 25 shots over the first two periods before Mike Dunham made his NHL debut and stopped seven of eight shots in the final period. Starting goalie Martin Brodeur was not with the team because his wife gave birth to twins earlier in the day.
Steve Thomas and Bobby Holik scored for the Devils.
In New York, Wayne Gretzky's power-play goal with less than five minutes remaining lifted the New York Rangers into a 1-1 tie with the Florida Panthers, the league's lone unbeaten team.
The goal extended Gretzky's point-scoring streak to 12 games. He has six goals and 12 assists in that span.

With the game scoreless in the third period, Ray Sheppard took a pass from Martin Straka at the top of the slot. Sheppard fired a blast that Dave Lowry tipped past Glenn Healy for his fourth goal of the season at 3:29.
"There are a lot of positive things about tonight. We worked hard, we just did not score," said Rangers coach Colin Campbell.
At Tampa Bay, Eric Weinrich's second goal of the game 6:50 into the third period lifted the Chicago Blackhawks into a 2-2 tie with the Tampa Bay Lightning.

Ethan Moreau carried the puck through the right circle and put a shot on goal that deflected off a maze of players in front. The rebound came to Weinrich in the slot, where he one-timed a shot past goaltender Corey Schwab for his fourth goal of the season.
The Blackhawks dominated the overtime, outshooting the Lightning 5-1, but Schwab preserved the tie with a pair of tough saves.
Dino Ciccarelli had both goals for the Lightning.

In Toronto, Ed Olczyk's power-play goal with 4:18 remaining snapped a tie and Ray Ferraro scored twice as the Los Angeles Kings ended a four-game winless streak with a 5-2 victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs.
The Maple Leafs carried a 2-1 lead into the third period, but Vladimir Tsyplakov tied it with his second goal of the season 2:05 into the period.
With Toronto's Jamie Macoun serving a hooking penalty, Olczyk put the Kings ahead to stay with 4:18 left.
Ferraro's second goal of the game with 1:44 to play made it 4-2. Yanic Perrault scored into an empty net with 15 seconds left to close the scoring.
